title: Sinking Profits Turn China’s $3.5 Trillion Stock Rout Into Trap
reason: 利润下滑令中国3.5万亿美元股市暴跌变成价值陷阱
summary: 中国股市自 5 月高点已蒸发 3.5 万亿美元，沪深 300 跌入熊市。核心问题是盈利：消费长期疲软和企业内卷压低利润，MSCI 中国成分股 2026 年盈利预期自 3 月以来下调逾 4%，已公布业绩的公司平均低于预期 9%，恒生科技盈利预期下调超 13%。市场判断经济“慢但可容忍”，北京不急于出台强刺激，因此看不到止跌信号。

paragraphs.text: Pessimism has gripped Chinese stocks, with no end in sight for a deepening selloff as investors confront the realities of an economy that’s weak enough to erode corporate profits but not to trigger forceful new stimulus.

The world’s second-largest equities market has lost $3.5 trillion in value from a peak in May, data compiled by Bloomberg show. The rout intensified last week, pushing the onshore benchmark CSI 300 Index into a bear market and a technology sector gauge in Hong Kong toward erasing all its gains since Beijing’s sweeping growth support package two years ago.

At the heart of investor gloom is an unsettling realization that a protracted consumption slump and the race-to-the-bottom mentality among businesses is taking a heavier toll on earnings across industries from banks to electric car makers and AI model developers. Further darkening the outlook is the growing perception that Chinese leaders are in no rush to jump-start an economy that is slowing but at a tolerable speed.

“It is too early to conclude that the worst is over,” said Ulrich Urbahn, head of multi-asset strategy and research at Berenberg. “The biggest concern remains profitability: China’s strength in production and exports is not translating consistently into stronger domestic demand, pricing power and corporate earnings.”

The third-quarter reporting season got off a disappointing start, with battery giant Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd., or CATL, suffering a profit miss that was symptomatic of both weak demand and fierce competition.

The consensus 2026 earnings forecasts for the MSCI China Index members has declined by over 4% since the end of March, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The Hang Seng Tech Index, dominated by Chinese Internet firms mired in e-commerce price wars, has seen profit projections plunge more than 13% during the period.

Yet even against the lowered expectations, the MSCI China’s constituents that have released results have missed consensus forecasts by an average of 9%, set for the second worst quarterly miss in two years, according to Bloomberg calculations.

Among them, AI infrastructure builder China Mobile Shares Fall After 9-Month Revenue, Profit Decline’s January-September net profit tumbled 8% on year amid cost pressures, while major materials firm Ganfeng Lithium Group Co. also Ganfeng Lithium Shares Fall After MS Sees 3Q Net Income Miss estimates on falling prices.

“CATL is the best poster child of what’s going on: great innovative company that’s doing great things but a victim of cut-throat competition and margin squeeze,” said Jason Lemire, chief investment officer at Bold Wealth Partners. “Competition is encouraged and generally brutal in China, not shareholder friendly.”

The earnings pressure has left companies, particularly China’s Internet behemoths that are in a tense race to fund costly AI infrastructure build-outs, increasingly out of cash. That has forced some of them to tap the equities market to raise funds, such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s $10 billion follow-on stock sale, which further diluted share value.

“I’d always weigh Japan, Korea and Taiwanese firms over China because they have better earnings,” said Stanley Tang, senior portfolio manager at Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management. “If you ask me what China can do, hard to think of any - even further localization of tech may not help to boost share prices.”

Weakening investor confidence is also showing up via other measures. Turnover in China’s onshore stock market is hovering near the lowest level since July last year, while the outstanding amount of margin trades — bets funded by borrowed cash — fell to the least in a year.
To be sure, the slumping market has already prompted authorities to mobilize state funds known as the national team to prevent stock prices from spiraling out of control.

Meanwhile, the recent rout has boosted the appeal of Chinese equities to some investors. Bridgewater Associates’ China arm, for one, said it has turned “prudently optimistic” on local stocks, saying the declines in the third quarter were largely driven by liquidity while valuations aren’t high. It also argued that policy favors long-term capital formation and more money may flow into equities given low bond yields.

Still, skepticism abounds that while the national team’s rescue efforts may be a temporary fix, the market’s long-term prospect remains dim given policymakers’ reluctance to adopt big-bang stimulus measures to accelerate economic growth.

China’s third-quarter gross domestic product grew 4.5% from a year ago, nudging expansion in the first nine months back into the government’s annual goal of 4.5%-5%. That target-meeting performance has given authorities more reason to stick to a drip-feed style of growth support, without compromising fiscal discipline or further reducing historically low borrowing costs.

“Policymakers are comfortable with the nature of economic growth,” said William Bratton, head of cash equity research for Asia Pacific at BNP Paribas. “As a result, either because they’re consciously keeping it in reserve or because philosophically they don’t believe in it, there’s no urgency to use fiscal measures to promote large scale consumption.”

annotations.explanation: grip 本义是“紧握”，新闻中常以情绪、恐慌、危机为主语，表示“笼罩、控制”某个市场或地区。

examples.en: Panic gripped the city after the earthquake.
examples.zh: 地震后，恐慌笼罩了整座城市。

annotations.meaningZh: 看不到尽头；没有结束的迹象
annotations.explanation: 常用于描述危机、冲突、下跌等负面局面将持续下去，作伴随状语。

examples.en: The strike continues with no end in sight.
examples.zh: 罢工仍在继续，看不到结束的迹象。

annotations.explanation: 金融新闻高频词，指投资者大量卖出导致价格下跌，也写作 sell-off。

examples.en: Tech stocks led the selloff on Monday.
examples.zh: 周一科技股领跌这轮抛售。

annotations.explanation: confront 指“正视、不得不面对”（通常是不愉快的事），比 face 语气更强。

examples.en: Retirees must confront the realities of rising healthcare costs.
examples.zh: 退休人员必须直面医疗费用上涨的现实。

annotations.explanation: 本义是“风化、侵蚀”，引申为利润、信心、优势等被逐渐削弱。常见搭配 erode profits / confidence / trust。

examples.en: Inflation has eroded the value of their savings.
examples.zh: 通货膨胀侵蚀了他们储蓄的价值。

annotations.explanation: 经济语境中指政府为提振经济推出的财政或货币刺激政策，常见 stimulus package / fiscal stimulus。

examples.en: The government announced a new stimulus to support consumption.
examples.zh: 政府宣布了一项新的刺激措施以支持消费。

target.text: Pessimism has gripped Chinese stocks, with no end in sight for a deepening selloff as investors confront the realities of an economy that’s weak enough to erode corporate profits but not to trigger forceful new stimulus.

annotations.translationZh: 悲观情绪笼罩着中国股市，愈演愈烈的抛售看不到尽头，因为投资者不得不面对这样的现实：经济疲弱到足以侵蚀企业利润，却又没弱到足以触发有力的新刺激措施。
annotations.explanation: 主句后接 with 引导的复合结构作伴随状语，再由 as 引出原因；定语从句中 weak enough to A but not (weak enough) to B 是省略结构，表达“弱到足以……却不足以……”的微妙对比。

examples.en: The job pays enough to cover rent but not to save anything.
examples.zh: 这份工作的收入够付房租，却不够存钱。

annotations.explanation: 复数 equities 在金融语境中指“股票”，equities market 即股票市场；单数 equity 也可指“股本、净资产”。

examples.en: She moved most of her savings into equities.
examples.zh: 她把大部分积蓄投入了股票。

annotations.explanation: 新闻常见的信息来源句式，置于句末作插入说明；注意 data 在正式语体中作复数，谓语用 show。

examples.en: Sales fell 5% last month, figures compiled by the agency show.
examples.zh: 该机构汇编的数据显示，上月销售额下降了 5%。

annotations.explanation: 本义是军事上的“溃败”，金融新闻中指市场大幅、全面下跌，语气比 decline 强烈得多。

examples.en: The bond rout wiped billions off pension funds.
examples.zh: 债市暴跌让养老基金蒸发了数十亿。

annotations.explanation: 谈中国市场时 onshore 指内地 A 股市场，与香港等 offshore（离岸）市场相对。

examples.en: Onshore yuan weakened against the dollar.
examples.zh: 在岸人民币兑美元走弱。

annotations.explanation: 指衡量整体市场表现的代表性指数，onshore benchmark CSI 300 即“境内基准指数沪深300”。

examples.zh: 基准指数收跌 2%。

annotations.explanation: 通常指指数从近期高点下跌 20% 以上；反义为 bull market（牛市）。

examples.zh: 分析师警告市场可能滑入熊市。

annotations.explanation: 本义是“测量仪表”，财经新闻中常用来指代某个指数或衡量指标，如 a technology sector gauge（科技板块指数）。

examples.zh: 一项消费者信心指标在六月上升。

annotations.explanation: 股市报道常用 erase / wipe out gains 表示把之前的涨幅全部跌回去。

examples.zh: 该股抹去了全年的全部涨幅。

annotations.explanation: 修饰改革、措施、变化等，表示范围广、力度大，如 sweeping reforms / changes。

examples.zh: 新法对税制进行了全面改革。

annotations.explanation: package 指“一揽子政策”，常见 stimulus package、rescue package。

annotations.explanation: 表示问题或现象的根本原因，常放句首引起倒装。

examples.zh: 这场争端的核心是薪酬分歧。

annotations.explanation: 本义“昏暗”，引申为情绪低落、前景暗淡，investor gloom 即“投资者的悲观情绪”。

examples.zh: 经济悲观情绪蔓延至整个欧洲。

annotations.explanation: 形容让人心神不宁、担忧的事物，比 worrying 略书面。

examples.en: It was an unsettling discovery.
examples.zh: 这是一个令人不安的发现。

annotations.explanation: 形容负面过程拖得很长，如 protracted negotiations / recession。

examples.en: The two sides ended a protracted legal battle.
examples.zh: 双方结束了一场旷日持久的官司。

annotations.explanation: 指销售、价格、经济活动的大幅、持续下滑，consumption slump 即“消费低迷”。

examples.en: The housing slump hurt construction firms.
examples.zh: 楼市低迷打击了建筑企业。

annotations.explanation: 指企业或地区通过不断压价、降标准来竞争，最终各方受损；中文常译“内卷式竞争”。连字符形式作定语。

examples.en: Critics say the price cuts have triggered a race to the bottom.
examples.zh: 批评人士说，降价引发了逐底竞争。

annotations.explanation: take a toll on 表示“造成损害”，加 heavy/heavier 强调程度。

examples.en: Long working hours took a heavy toll on her health.
examples.zh: 长时间工作严重损害了她的健康。

annotations.explanation: outlook 指“前景、展望”，darken 用作动词“使变暗”，财经新闻常见。

examples.en: Rising rates are darkening the outlook for home buyers.
examples.zh: 利率上升让购房者的前景更加暗淡。

annotations.lemma: be in no rush to do something
annotations.explanation: 等于 be in no hurry to do，表示不着急做某事，常暗含有意拖延。

examples.en: The company is in no rush to sell the unit.
examples.zh: 该公司并不急于出售这个部门。

annotations.explanation: 原指用跨接电缆启动汽车，引申为用强力措施让经济、项目重新运转。

examples.en: The new policy aims to jump-start the economy.
examples.zh: 新政策旨在提振经济。

annotations.meaningZh: 可以接受的；尚可忍受的
annotations.explanation: 表示“虽不理想但可接受”，at a tolerable speed 暗示官方对放缓并不焦虑。

examples.en: Prices rose at a tolerable pace.
examples.zh: 物价以可以接受的速度上涨。

target.text: At the heart of investor gloom is an unsettling realization that a protracted consumption slump and the race-to-the-bottom mentality among businesses is taking a heavier toll on earnings across industries from banks to electric car makers and AI model developers.

annotations.translationZh: 投资者悲观情绪的核心，在于一个令人不安的认识：旷日持久的消费低迷以及企业间的逐底竞争心态，正对从银行到电动车制造商再到 AI 模型开发商等各行业的盈利造成更沉重的打击。
annotations.explanation: 表语前置引起的完全倒装：正常语序是 An unsettling realization … is at the heart of investor gloom。主语很长，把短的表语提前使句子更平衡；that 引导同位语从句解释 realization。

annotations.explanation: 分词短语前置的倒装：Further darkening the outlook 作表语提前，真正主语是 the growing perception；这种结构常用于承接上句、递进补充。

examples.zh: 该基金采用多资产策略。

examples.zh: 公司专注于提升盈利能力。

examples.zh: 销量增加并没有转化为更高的利润。

annotations.explanation: 宏观经济术语，与 external demand（外需）相对。

annotations.explanation: 指企业提高价格而不流失客户的能力，是衡量竞争力的重要指标。

examples.en: Luxury brands enjoy strong pricing power.
examples.zh: 奢侈品牌拥有很强的定价权。

examples.zh: 随着财报季开始，投资者密切关注。

examples.zh: 这支球队本赛季开局缓慢。

examples.zh: 消息公布后油价骤降。

annotations.explanation: 财经报道的简写，等于 year on year（与去年同期相比）；环比为 on quarter / month on month。

examples.en: Retail sales rose 3% on year.
examples.zh: 零售额同比增长 3%。

annotations.explanation: amid 表示“在……的背景下”，新闻中常用来交代原因或环境。

examples.en: Shares fell amid concerns over demand.
examples.zh: 在对需求的担忧中，股价下跌。

annotations.explanation: 财经新闻中 on 可表示原因，如 rise on strong demand（因需求强劲而上涨）。

examples.en: The stock jumped on strong earnings.
examples.zh: 受强劲业绩推动，该股大涨。

annotations.explanation: 原指慈善海报上的代表儿童，引申为最能体现某现象的典型例子，褒贬均可。

examples.en: The city has become a poster child for urban renewal.
examples.zh: 这座城市已成为城市更新的典型代表。

annotations.explanation: 可用于抽象情形，表示因某种环境或趋势而受损，如 a victim of its own success。

examples.en: The shop was a victim of rising rents.
examples.zh: 这家店是租金上涨的牺牲品。

annotations.explanation: 字面“割喉的”，形容竞争极其激烈、不择手段。

examples.en: The airline industry is cut-throat.
examples.zh: 航空业竞争残酷。

annotations.explanation: margin 指利润率，squeeze 指挤压；成本上升或售价下降都会造成 margin squeeze。

examples.en: Retailers face a margin squeeze as wages rise.
examples.zh: 随着工资上涨，零售商面临利润率挤压。

annotations.explanation: 指重视股东回报（分红、回购等）的公司或政策，通常加连字符作定语。

examples.en: The company has adopted more shareholder-friendly policies.
examples.zh: 公司采取了更多对股东友好的政策。

annotations.explanation: 源自《圣经》中的巨兽，常指规模庞大的公司。

examples.en: Tech behemoths dominate online advertising.
examples.zh: 科技巨头主导了网络广告。

annotations.lemma: be in a race to do something
annotations.explanation: race to do 表示“争相做某事”，tense 突出紧张激烈。

examples.en: Automakers are in a race to build cheaper batteries.
examples.zh: 汽车商正争相制造更便宜的电池。

annotations.explanation: 指基础设施、网络、数据中心等的扩建工程，科技新闻常用。

examples.en: The 5G build-out will take years.
examples.zh: 5G 网络建设将需要数年。

annotations.explanation: out of 表示“用完、缺少”，increasingly out of cash 即“现金日益紧张”。

examples.en: Many startups ran out of cash during the downturn.
examples.zh: 经济低迷期间许多初创公司现金耗尽。

annotations.explanation: tap 本义“开发、利用（资源）”，金融中 tap the bond/equity market 指到该市场融资。

examples.en: The firm tapped the bond market for $2 billion.
examples.zh: 该公司在债券市场融资 20 亿美元。

annotations.explanation: 指已上市公司再次发行新股融资，区别于首次公开募股 IPO。

examples.en: The bank arranged a follow-on stock sale for the company.
examples.zh: 该银行为公司安排了一次增发。

annotations.explanation: 本义“稀释（液体）”，金融中指增发新股使每股价值或持股比例下降。

examples.en: Issuing new shares diluted existing holders.
examples.zh: 发行新股稀释了现有股东的权益。

target.text: The earnings pressure has left companies, particularly China’s Internet behemoths that are in a tense race to fund costly AI infrastructure build-outs, increasingly out of cash.

annotations.translationZh: 盈利压力使企业——尤其是正争相投入巨资建设 AI 基础设施的中国互联网巨头——现金日益紧张。
annotations.explanation: leave + 宾语 + 补足语结构（leave companies out of cash），中间插入 particularly… 进一步说明宾语，导致宾语与补足语相隔很远，阅读时要把首尾对应起来。

structure.text: The earnings pressure
has left
companies
particularly China’s Internet behemoths that are in a tense race to fund costly AI infrastructure build-outs
increasingly out of cash

examples.en: The long trip left everyone exhausted.
examples.zh: 长途旅行让每个人都筋疲力尽。

target.text: weigh Japan, Korea and Taiwanese firms over China

annotations.meaningZh: 更偏好日韩台企业而非中国企业
annotations.explanation: 这里 weigh A over B 指在投资配置中“更看重 A 而非 B”，与 overweight（超配）概念相近。

examples.en: Many funds weigh US stocks over European ones.
examples.zh: 许多基金更偏好美股而非欧股。

annotations.meaningZh: 投资组合经理；基金经理
annotations.explanation: 资产管理行业职位，负责管理基金或投资组合。

examples.en: She works as a portfolio manager at a hedge fund.
examples.zh: 她在一家对冲基金担任投资组合经理。

annotations.explanation: 此处 localization of tech 指技术国产替代，而非软件“本地化”。

examples.en: The government is pushing chip localization.
examples.zh: 政府正在推动芯片国产化。

target.text: If you ask me what China can do, hard to think of any - even further localization of tech may not help to boost share prices.

annotations.translationZh: 如果你问我中国能做些什么，我很难想出任何办法——即便进一步推进技术国产化，也未必有助于提振股价。
annotations.explanation: 口语化省略：hard to think of any 省略了主语和系动词 It’s，any 后省略 measures/thing；破折号后补充说明理由。

structure.text: If you ask me what China can do
hard to think of any
structure.note: = It’s hard to think of any

structure.text: even further localization of tech may not help to boost share prices

examples.en: If you ask me what China can do, it’s hard to think of anything.
examples.zh: （完整形式）如果你问我中国能做什么，很难想出任何办法。

annotations.explanation: show up 除“出席”外，还表示“显现、被看出”。

examples.en: The effects of the policy are starting to show up in the data.
examples.zh: 政策效果开始在数据中显现。

annotations.explanation: 熟词僻义：measure 常指“措施”，此处指“衡量标准、指标”。

examples.en: GDP is one measure of economic health.
examples.zh: GDP 是衡量经济健康的指标之一。

annotations.explanation: 在股市语境指成交量/成交额，在公司语境可指营业额或人员流动率。

examples.en: Daily turnover hit a record.
examples.zh: 日成交额创纪录。

annotations.explanation: 本义“盘旋”，引申为数值在某水平附近小幅波动。

examples.en: Unemployment is hovering around 5%.
examples.zh: 失业率在 5% 左右徘徊。

annotations.explanation: outstanding 在金融中意为“未偿还的”，不是“杰出的”。

examples.en: The outstanding amount of the loan is $50,000.
examples.zh: 这笔贷款的未偿余额为 5 万美元。

annotations.explanation: 指借钱买股票（杠杆交易），破折号内正好给出解释 bets funded by borrowed cash。

examples.en: Regulators tightened rules on margin trading.
examples.zh: 监管机构收紧了融资交易规则。

target.text: fell to the least in a year

annotations.lemma: fall to the least/lowest in + 时间
annotations.explanation: 新闻常用比较表达，in a year 表示“一年以来”。

examples.en: Applications fell to the lowest in a decade.
examples.zh: 申请数量降至十年来最低。

target.text: Turnover in China’s onshore stock market is hovering near the lowest level since July last year, while the outstanding amount of margin trades — bets funded by borrowed cash — fell to the least in a year.

annotations.translationZh: 中国境内股市成交额在去年 7 月以来的最低水平附近徘徊，而融资交易（即用借来的钱下注）余额则降至一年来最低。
annotations.explanation: while 连接两个并列对比的分句；破折号之间是同位语，解释 margin trades 的含义，是新闻中解释术语的常见手法。

structure.text: Turnover in China’s onshore stock market is hovering near the lowest level since July last year
while
the outstanding amount of margin trades
bets funded by borrowed cash
fell to the least in a year

examples.en: Bitcoin — a digital currency with no central bank — fell sharply.
examples.zh: 比特币——一种没有央行的数字货币——大幅下跌。

annotations.explanation: 用于先承认某个事实或对立观点，后文常接转折，相当于 admittedly。

examples.en: To be sure, the plan has its flaws.
examples.zh: 诚然，这个计划有其缺陷。

annotations.explanation: prompt 作动词意为“促使、引发”。

examples.en: The scandal prompted the CEO to resign.
examples.zh: 丑闻促使首席执行官辞职。

annotations.explanation: 指调集资源或人员用于特定目的，如 mobilize funds / troops。

examples.en: The charity mobilized volunteers after the flood.
examples.zh: 洪水后该慈善机构动员了志愿者。

annotations.explanation: 特定背景含义：指为稳定中国股市而入市的国有资金（如汇金、证金等），非体育“国家队”。

examples.en: The national team bought ETFs to support the market.
examples.zh: 国家队买入 ETF 以托市。

annotations.explanation: 固定搭配 prevent A from doing B。

examples.en: Rules prevent employees from trading company stock.
examples.zh: 规定禁止员工交易公司股票。

annotations.explanation: spiral 指“螺旋式（加速）变化”，形容局面越来越糟直至失控。

examples.en: Costs began spiraling out of control.
examples.zh: 成本开始失控。

annotations.explanation: appeal 作名词指“吸引力”，常与 boost / lose / broaden 搭配。

examples.en: Lower prices boosted the appeal of electric cars.
examples.zh: 价格下降提升了电动车的吸引力。

annotations.explanation: 熟词僻义：arm 在商业语境中指公司的分支或业务部门。

examples.en: The bank’s investment arm reported strong profits.
examples.zh: 该银行的投资部门利润强劲。

annotations.explanation: 放在主语后，表示举出一个例子，暗示还有其他人持同样看法。

examples.en: Many people liked the idea. Sarah, for one, was thrilled.
examples.zh: 很多人喜欢这个主意，比如萨拉就非常兴奋。

annotations.explanation: prudently 意为“谨慎地”，常见说法为 cautiously optimistic。

examples.en: Analysts remain cautiously optimistic about growth.
examples.zh: 分析师对增长保持审慎乐观。

annotations.explanation: 金融术语，指资金充裕程度或资产变现的难易。

examples.en: The central bank injected liquidity into the market.
examples.zh: 央行向市场注入流动性。

annotations.explanation: 指对公司或资产价值的评估，valuations aren’t high 即“估值不高”。

examples.en: Tech valuations look stretched.
examples.zh: 科技股估值显得过高。

annotations.explanation: 经济学术语，指社会资本的积累与投入。

examples.en: Tax incentives can encourage capital formation.
examples.zh: 税收激励可以促进资本形成。

annotations.explanation: given 作介词表原因，等于 considering。

examples.en: Given the weather, the event was cancelled.
examples.zh: 鉴于天气原因，活动取消了。

annotations.explanation: 债券收益率低时，资金可能转向股票寻求更高回报。

examples.en: Bond yields fell to record lows.
examples.zh: 债券收益率跌至历史低点。

annotations.explanation: 表示某事物很多，主语多为 rumors、skepticism、opportunities 等。

examples.en: Rumors abound about his resignation.
examples.zh: 关于他辞职的传言满天飞。

annotations.meaningZh: 权宜之计；临时解决办法
annotations.explanation: fix 作名词指“解决办法”，temporary fix 暗示治标不治本。

examples.en: The repair is only a temporary fix.
examples.zh: 这次修理只是权宜之计。

annotations.explanation: 本义“昏暗的”，修饰 prospect 时指“前景渺茫”。

examples.en: Hopes of a deal look dim.
examples.zh: 达成协议的希望很渺茫。

annotations.explanation: 常见 reluctance to do something。

examples.en: Banks showed reluctance to lend.
examples.zh: 银行不愿放贷。

annotations.meaningZh: 大规模一次性的；大刀阔斧的
annotations.explanation: 源自“宇宙大爆炸”，形容一次性、力度极大的政策或改革。

examples.en: The government ruled out a big-bang reform.
examples.zh: 政府排除了激进式改革的可能。

target.text: Still, skepticism abounds that while the national team’s rescue efforts may be a temporary fix, the market’s long-term prospect remains dim given policymakers’ reluctance to adopt big-bang stimulus measures to accelerate economic growth.

annotations.translationZh: 尽管如此，怀疑情绪仍普遍存在：虽然国家队的救市举措或许能暂时止跌，但鉴于决策者不愿推出大规模刺激措施来加速经济增长，市场的长期前景依然黯淡。
annotations.explanation: 同位语从句后置：that 从句解释 skepticism 的内容，却被谓语 abounds 隔开，以免头重脚轻；从句内部又含 while 让步从句和 given 引导的原因短语。

structure.text: Still
skepticism abounds
that while the national team’s rescue efforts may be a temporary fix
the market’s long-term prospect remains dim
given policymakers’ reluctance to adopt big-bang stimulus measures to accelerate economic growth

examples.en: News came that the plan had been approved.
examples.zh: 传来消息说计划已获批准。

annotations.explanation: 本义“用肘轻推”，引申为小幅推动某数值或某人朝某方向变化。

examples.en: Higher fuel costs nudged inflation up.
examples.zh: 燃料成本上升推高了通胀。

annotations.explanation: 表示坚持既定计划、做法或原则。

examples.en: We decided to stick to the original plan.
examples.zh: 我们决定坚持原计划。

annotations.meaningZh: 细水长流式的；一点点给予的
annotations.explanation: 原指“点滴输液”，引申为分批少量地提供资金或支持。

examples.en: The government drip-fed funds to the project.
examples.zh: 政府分批少量地向该项目拨款。

annotations.explanation: 熟词僻义：compromise 除“妥协”外，还表示“损害、危及”，如 compromise security。

examples.en: Cutting costs should not compromise safety.
examples.zh: 削减成本不应以牺牲安全为代价。

annotations.explanation: 指控制赤字和债务的审慎财政原则。

examples.en: The minister stressed the need for fiscal discipline.
examples.zh: 部长强调财政纪律的必要性。

annotations.explanation: 通常指利率水平，historically low borrowing costs 即“处于历史低位的利率”。

examples.en: Rising borrowing costs hurt home buyers.
examples.zh: 借贷成本上升打击了购房者。

target.text: That target-meeting performance has given authorities more reason to stick to a drip-feed style of growth support, without compromising fiscal discipline or further reducing historically low borrowing costs.

annotations.translationZh: 这一达标的表现让当局更有理由坚持细水长流式的增长支持，而不必牺牲财政纪律，也不必进一步下调已处于历史低位的借贷成本。
annotations.explanation: give sb reason to do 结构；without + 动名词 表示“而不……”，两个动名词由 or 并列。

structure.text: That target-meeting performance
has given authorities more reason
to stick to a drip-feed style of growth support
without compromising fiscal discipline or further reducing historically low borrowing costs

examples.en: The good results gave the team more reason to keep going.
examples.zh: 好成绩让团队更有理由坚持下去。

annotations.explanation: 表示对现状没有不安、可以接受。

examples.en: The board is comfortable with the current strategy.
examples.zh: 董事会对当前战略感到满意。

annotations.explanation: 投行术语，指直接买卖股票本身，区别于衍生品。

examples.en: He leads the cash equity trading desk.
examples.zh: 他领导现货股票交易部门。

annotations.explanation: in reserve 表示“备用、储备”。

examples.en: We kept some money in reserve for emergencies.
examples.zh: 我们存了一些钱以备急需。

annotations.meaningZh: 从理念上；从根本观念上
annotations.explanation: 这里不是“哲学上”，而是指出于基本理念或信念。

examples.en: Philosophically, she opposes big government.
examples.zh: 从理念上讲，她反对大政府。

annotations.lemma: there is no urgency to do something
annotations.explanation: 表示没有必要急于做某事。

examples.en: There is no urgency to decide today.
examples.zh: 今天不急于做决定。

target.text: As a result, either because they’re consciously keeping it in reserve or because philosophically they don’t believe in it, there’s no urgency to use fiscal measures to promote large scale consumption.

annotations.translationZh: 因此，要么是因为他们有意留作后手，要么是因为他们在理念上不认同这种做法，总之他们并不急于动用财政手段去推动大规模消费。
annotations.explanation: either because… or because… 并列两个原因状语从句，置于主句之前；主句为 there be 句型。

structure.text: As a result
either because they’re consciously keeping it in reserve
or because philosophically they don’t believe in it
there’s no urgency to use fiscal measures to promote large scale consumption

examples.en: Either because he was tired or because he was bored, he left early.
examples.zh: 不知是累了还是无聊了，他提早离开了。
